correctness.rationale: An idempotent over a finite commutative local ring splits a free module into free image/kernel summands. Pairwise commuting idempotents have pairwise orthogonal binary-pattern projections P_epsilon; every ordered decomposition into 2^k labelled free summands gives exactly one tuple. The GL_n(R) action has product GL_{r_eps}(R) stabilizer and |GL_j(R)|=(s/q)^(j^2)|GL_j(F_q)|. Partition-lattice signed-Stirling inversion removes repeated tuple entries; a maximal Boolean algebra of projections must refine to n rank-one free summands, giving 2^n and g_n/(n!g_1^n). In dimension two noncentral rank-one projections commute only with complements: graph K_2 join a matching. Independent direct matrix enumeration over F_2 and Z/4Z yielded 8 and 26 idempotents, and exactly 3 and 12 edges among noncentral idempotents, matching formulas; the finite checks do not replace freeness or simultaneous splitting proof.

evidence: Known local-ring idempotent number I_n is exactly the present k=1 specialization; general commuting-idempotent lifting results do not provide coefficientwise clique number for every n and k.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The broadest inspected theorems are structural, not an all-tuple graph polynomial. Such existing general facts must not be represented as newly discovered.

originality.rationale: Dolžan covers single idempotents; module-freeness and simultaneous decomposition are classical. The complete all-arity local-ring clique polynomial, exact maximal-family count, and dependence only on ring size and residue-field size were not found in inspected primary material. The claim does not assert full graph isomorphism for n>2; the k=1 case and field-pair counts are prior.

value.rationale: The entire clique polynomial of an algebraically defined graph is a natural but generally difficult graph invariant. The result proves ring-size universality and a complete maximal-clique count in all dimensions and for nonprincipal local rings, not just a routine individual-idempotent count; higher-arity data may aid comparisons of commuting graphs.
